text:
Alex K: Quick experiment notes — noticed a ~12% p95 regression when streaming + continuous batching after a kernel-hint change.
Maya R: which kernel-hint change? commit/sha?
Alex K: rolled patch that prefers larger matmul kernel for fused-attn on A100 when seq<=512 (commit 9f3a2b). seemed good for throughput.
Sanjay P: hmm that could affect the partial-decode path — larger kernels sometimes require extra stream-syncs for small microbatches.
Lina (infra-bot): perf-ci queued: run/4829 started (profile + flamegraph) https://ci/redwood/runs/4829
Jamie T: Data from run/4829: baseline streaming p50 18ms -> new 22ms; batch formation latency up ~3.4ms; token emit time increased.
Alex K: KV cache hit ratio is unchanged, but prefix fetch time increased ~1.1ms — looks like kernel handoff blocks the prefetch step in some cases.
Maya R: do we have queue-depth / per-queue timing breakdown? maybe the token-budget policy increased effective batch window for these flows.
Sanjay P: attaching top stacks from the flamegraph:
```text
# top stacks (decode)
decode_loop -> schedule_partial_decode -> kernel_select -> launch_matmul_large
launch_matmul_large waiting on stream-sync
```
Jamie T: observed that when clients request small streaming tokens and we hold for batch-window=1.5ms, the partial-decode scheduling ends up waiting for matmul resources to be setup.
Alex K: hypothesis: choosing the larger matmul kernel improves throughput on large batches but increases tail for low-latency streaming because of kernel startup / stream-sync overhead.
Maya R: quick mitigation idea: add a "streaming-friendly" kernel hint that prefers the smaller-kernel path when request.metadata.streaming==true or token_budget < X.
Sanjay P: microbench: switching to small-kernel for streaming decreased p95 by ~9% and restored p50 to ~17ms. Tradeoff: overall throughput dropped ~2.8% on pure throughput workloads.
Jamie T: proposal: dynamic policy — kernel hint per-queue based on recent streaming fraction. if stream_frac > 0.3 prefer small-kernel; otherwise keep default.
Alex K: also tweak batch formation: for streaming-labeled requests, use greedy immediate-flush for partial-decode-eligible items instead of waiting full token-budget window. reduces tail.
Maya R: implemented canary config: `batcher.streaming_mode=true`, `partial_decode_timeout_ms=0.6`, `kernel_hint_override=small_if_streaming`. rolled to canary on ded-1.
Lina (infra-bot): canary metrics: ded-1 canary/streaming-friendly run: qps stable; errors 0; dashboards: https://dash/redwood/canary/ded-1
Jamie T: canary results: streaming p95 down ~11%, non-streaming throughput drop ~1.5% under mixed synthetic 30% streaming / 70% batch mix.
Sanjay P: one concern: KV cache prefetch sometimes races with the small-kernel path and triggers an extra memcpy; that adds a few hundred microseconds. we should gate prefetch.
Alex K: proposed: only prefetch when batch_size >= 2 OR request.flags.cold_kv == true. add instrumentation counter `prefetch_gated`.
Maya R: will add tracing: include `kernel_choice` tag and `token_budget_target` histogram in traces so we can correlate kernel_choice -> tail.
Jamie T: also add a perf-ci mixed-workload regression test that runs streaming+batch mix, toggles kernel_hint, and asserts p95 < threshold.
Alex K: I'll open a PR with the config, the canary rollout plan, the prefetch gate, and the perf-ci test. tagging @Maya @Sanjay for review.
Sanjay P: ack — will review tomorrow morning.
Maya R: thanks. small note: ensure fallback to large-kernel if small-kernel OOMs on quantized models (we hit that previously).
Alex K: good catch — adding fallback logic and a short-circuit in kernel_select to revert on memory pressure.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled to canary cluster ded-1 at 2024-02-02T03:00:00Z :rocket:
Jamie T: Nice. Let's reconvene after full canary window and the perf-ci run. :thumbsup:
